s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive visual impairment with endocrinological disturbances and a sellar/suprasellar mass
salient_findings: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm
key_facts: 2-week history of rapidly progressive visual reduction
Vestibular schwannoma treated by gamma-knife radiosurgery 2 years earlier
Mass compressing the optic chiasm and extending toward the left cavernous sinus
Lesion predominantly isointense to gray matter on T1-weighted images
Diffuse homogeneous enhancement after contrast administration
Normal pituitary gland on previous MRI

raw.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive visual impairment with endocrinological disturbances and a sellar/suprasellar mass
salient_findings: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm
key_facts: 2-week history of rapidly progressive visual reduction

shortlist.label: Pituitary macroadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm and elevated prolactin level

shortlist.label: Craniopharyngioma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive visual reduction and sellar/suprasellar mass

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass and history of vestibular schwannoma

shortlist.label: Pituitary carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid growth of sellar/suprasellar mass and abnormal endocrinological evaluation

shortlist.label: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive visual reduction and endocrinological disturbances

raw.rationale: The patient's rapidly progressive visual reduction, bitemporal hemianopsia, and sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm are consistent with a pituitary macroadenoma. The lesion's imaging characteristics, including its size, location, and enhancement pattern, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Craniopharyngioma
rejected.why: Less likely due to the absence of characteristic cystic components on MRI

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Less likely due to the location and imaging characteristics, which are more typical of a pituitary macroadenoma

rejected.label: Pituitary carcinoma
rejected.why: Less likely due to the lack of evidence of metastatic disease or invasive growth

rejected.label: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
rejected.why: Less likely due to the presence of a discrete sellar/suprasellar mass, which is not typical of this condition
